title: Director of Customer Enterprise Transformation Consulting at Cognizant Technology Solutions Believes AI Is Reshaping IT Services and Talent Dynamics
expert: Director of Customer Enterprise Transformation Consulting at Cognizant (competitor; listed as former by GenSearch; 40 years in IT integration); interview 2026-08-07
verdict: A Cognizant transformation director (competitor, interviewed 2026-08-07) gives no TCS figures: he hears TCS staffs projects with juniors and sees 1 in 5 AI efforts failing today, possibly 4 in 5 (estimates), as $112-per-hour billing gives way to outcome pricing.

Non-AI revenue trend: 🔴 First-level call-centre work "gone now almost everywhere" to AI agents; consistent with TCS non-AI revenue -1.5% q/q in 2QFY27 (SB #62834). → Tenet 1 (AI deflates core) ↑ {c12}
🔴 $112 per person per hour billing expected to disappear for outcome-based pricing (hearsay) vs mgmt "no pricing pressure" (SB #62847): conflicting. → Tenet 1 (AI deflates core) ↑ {c4}
EBIT margin and the 25% exit: 🟡 1 in 5 AI efforts failing today, could become 4 in 5 (estimate): delivery risk on AI work now US$3.1bn annualised (SB #62809). → Tenet 5 (AI-native competition) ↑ {c5}

changes: Call-centre work lost to AI agents vs TCS non-AI revenue -1.5% q/q, US$6,867m (SB #62834): consistent.
Hourly billing giving way to outcome pricing vs mgmt "no pricing pressure; portfolio pricing stable" (SB #62847, 2026-10-09): conflicting.
First read on AI project failure rates (1 in 5 now); no earlier expert call or stored row.
thesis_impact: Tenet 1 (AI deflates the non-AI core): ↑ — first-level call-centre work gone to AI agents; $112/hour billing to give way to outcome pricing.
Tenet 5 (AI-native competition): ↑ — specialist boutiques and onshore regional compounds gain on GSIs; TCS seen deploying juniors without senior leads.
Tenet 2 (EBIT ~24%): → — talent gap for 0–3 years' experience hires noted, no margin figure.
